A.explanation: This is about half of $9.3\text{ N m}$. It comes from using the labelled radius instead of the full separation $2r$ between the two forces of each couple.

B.explanation: This is about half of $17.1\text{ N m}$. It uses $\text{torque} = F \times r$ instead of $F \times 2r$ for every $16\text{ N}$, $25\text{ N}$, $30\text{ N}$ and $50\text{ N}$ couple.

C.explanation: Resultant is $6.0 + 3.2 + 4.0 - 3.9 = 9.3\text{ N m}$ because the $30\text{ N}$ couple opposes the other three couples.

D.explanation: This adds all four magnitudes $6.0 + 3.2 + 3.9 + 4.0 = 17.1\text{ N m}$ and ignores that the $30\text{ N}$ up-down pair twists opposite to the $16\text{ N}$, $25\text{ N}$ and $50\text{ N}$ pairs.

hints: Notice each pair shown is a couple: two equal, opposite, parallel forces, so use $\text{torque of couple} = F \times \text{separation}$ for the $50\text{ N}$, $30\text{ N}$, $16\text{ N}$ and $25\text{ N}$ pairs.

The dashed $4.0\text{ cm}$, $6.5\text{ cm}$, $10\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$ are radii to the centre, so the separation for each couple is twice the value, for example $0.080\text{ m}$ for the $50\text{ N}$ pair.

Compare twisting senses: the left-up and right-down $30\text{ N}$ forces give a clockwise twist, while the $16\text{ N}$, $25\text{ N}$ and $50\text{ N}$ pairs give the opposite twist, so subtract the $30\text{ N}$ torque from the sum of the other three.
walkthrough: Identify the four couples and their radii from the diagram: $50\text{ N}$ at $4.0\text{ cm}$, $30\text{ N}$ at $6.5\text{ cm}$, $16\text{ N}$ at $10\text{ cm}$, $25\text{ N}$ at $12\text{ cm}$.

State the rule for one couple: $\text{torque} = F \times \text{perpendicular separation}$. Because the two forces are on opposite sides of the centre, separation $= 2r$. Convert $\text{cm}$ to $\text{m}$.

Calculate each magnitude: $50\text{ N}$ couple $= 50 \times 0.080 = 4.0\text{ N m}$; $30\text{ N}$ couple $= 30 \times 0.130 = 3.9\text{ N m}$; $16\text{ N}$ couple $= 16 \times 0.200 = 3.2\text{ N m}$; $25\text{ N}$ couple $= 25 \times 0.240 = 6.0\text{ N m}$.

Decide direction about the centre. The $30\text{ N}$ left force up and right force down both produce clockwise moments, while the $50\text{ N}$, $16\text{ N}$ and $25\text{ N}$ pairs both produce anticlockwise moments.
Take anticlockwise as positive: $T = +4.0 + 3.2 + 6.0 - 3.9 = +9.3\text{ N m}$. The magnitude of resultant torque is $9.3\text{ N m}$. This is option C.
